headline: GOLD CRATERS TO $4,500, SILVER DOWN 7% — INFLATION SHOCK WIPES BILLIONS FROM MINING STOCKS
snippet: Spot gold fell 2% to $4,552 an ounce and silver plunged 6.5% to $78 on May 15 as hot US CPI and PPI data reignited inflation fears and killed near-term Fed rate-cut hopes. Junior mining stocks took heavy losses — Silvercorp Metals down 6.9%, Teck Resources off 5.9%, Endeavour Silver down 4.9% — while gold futures wiped out all gains from the prior two trading weeks. Gold has retreated nearly 20% from its January record near $5,600.

headline: TRUMP-XI SUMMIT FALLOUT: BONDS, METALS AND MINING STOCKS SLUMP AS U.S. INFLATION KILLS RATE-CUT HOPES
snippet: Global risk assets sold off sharply on May 15 as Trump concluded his China summit and markets absorbed accelerating US inflation data. The dollar index rose 0.4%, oil jumped on a reported China oil-buying agreement, and the combination torpedoed precious metals and mining equities. US wholesale inflation surged at its fastest pace since 2022 in April, while consumer prices posted their largest monthly increase since 2023.

headline: $18.5B DEAL: EQUINOX SWALLOWS ORLA MINING TO FORGE NORTH AMERICA'S NEW SENIOR GOLD PRODUCER
snippet: Equinox Gold will acquire Orla Mining in a cash-and-stock deal valued at US$5.1 billion, creating a combined entity with an $18.5 billion market cap and expected annual production of 1.1 million ounces of gold — with a funded path to 1.9 million oz. Equinox shareholders retain 67% of the merged company; Orla holders receive 33%. The deal, anchored by three long-life Canadian mines including Greenstone and Valentine, heads to shareholder votes in July 2026.

headline: HEMLO MINING HITS 16 G/T GOLD OVER 8 METRES — HIGH-GRADE ZONE FOUND 50M FROM ACTIVE PIT
snippet: Hemlo Mining Corp. (TSXV: HMMC) reported 16.1 g/t Au over 8.1 metres — including a 59.7 g/t bonanza intercept over 2 metres — from the newly interpreted South-Rim Zone at the historic Hemlo gold district in northern Ontario. All seven completed holes in the 20-hole program intersected mineralization. The zone sits 50–150 metres from the actively mining C-Zone, pointing to a near-term, low-capital resource growth option within the 130,000-metre 2026 drill program.

headline: SOUTH32-BACKED RIDGELINE MINERALS DRILLS NEVADA CRD SILVER DISCOVERY WITH $12M PARTNER BUDGET
snippet: Ridgeline Minerals (TSXV: RDG) initiated its 2026 partner-funded drill program at the Chinchilla Sulfide CRD discovery at the Selena project in Nevada, backed by a South32 earn-in worth US$4.4 million for Year 3 alone. The exploration target spans 38–58 million tonnes grading 40–52 g/t silver with gold, lead and zinc credits. Total 2026 partner-funded budgets across Ridgeline's Nevada portfolio reach $12 million — the largest in company history.

headline: PREMIER AMERICAN URANIUM KICKS OFF 100,000-FOOT DRILL CAMPAIGN IN WYOMING'S POWDER RIVER BASIN
snippet: Premier American Uranium (TSXV: PUR) commenced its 2026 exploration drill program at the wholly-owned Kaycee ISR project in Wyoming's Powder River Basin — one of the few uranium projects where all three historically productive sandstone formations (Wasatch, Fort Union, and Lance) are mineralized and accessible for in-situ recovery. The 100,000-foot program targets the Outpost and Rustler zones across a 46-square-mile, 110-mile mineralized trend. Uranium spot sits at ~$86/lb, up 20% year-over-year.

headline: USA RARE EARTH Q1: FIRST YTTRIUM PRODUCTION, $2.8B BRAZIL ACQUISITION — STOCK UP 115% YTD
snippet: USA Rare Earth (NYSE: USAR) reported Q1 2026 milestones including first commercial yttrium production at LCM, commissioning of Stillwater Phase 1a, full acquisition of Texas Mineral Resources, and a planned $2.8 billion acquisition of Serra Verde in Brazil. The stock is up 114% year to date and 191% over the past year, underpinned by rising US government demand for domestically sourced critical minerals and the company's vertically integrated rare earth processing strategy.

headline: FORGET MP MATERIALS: THE RARE EARTH PLAYS WITH $354M IN PENTAGON CONTRACTS AND GREENLAND'S BIGGEST DEPOSIT
snippet: US Antimony (NYSE: UAMY) holds $354 million in signed Pentagon and Defense Production Act contracts with CEO guidance for $125 million in 2026 revenue — up 163% year-over-year — and the stock is up 274% over the past year. Critical Metals Corp. (NASDAQ: CRML) controls 92.5% of the Tanbreez heavy rare earth project in Greenland, the largest such deposit outside China, backed by a $120 million US EXIM Bank letter of intent. Both present Western supply-chain alternatives to dominant MP Materials.

headline: COPPER SINKS TO $6.30/LB ON CHINA DEMAND STALL — U.S. 25% TARIFF RECOMMENDATION DUE BEFORE JUNE
snippet: Copper futures fell to near $6.30 per pound on May 15, a second straight session of losses, as elevated prices discouraged Chinese buying and the broader commodity selloff deepened. Goldman Sachs's base case is that the US Commerce Secretary will recommend a copper import tariff of at least 25% to the White House before June 2026. Despite the pullback, analysts view the long-term demand outlook — driven by AI infrastructure, grid modernisation, and clean energy — as structurally intact.

headline: LITHIUM UP 197% IN A YEAR AS ZIMBABWE BANS RAW EXPORTS AND AI DATA CENTERS BUILD NEW DEMAND
snippet: Lithium carbonate prices are up 197% year-over-year and 14.6% over the past month, driven by tightening Chinese supply policy, surging energy storage demand, and new buying from AI data-centre operators whose grid-scale storage systems require more lithium than EVs. Energy storage is projected to account for 31% of lithium consumption in 2026, up from 23% in 2025. Zimbabwe has imposed quotas on raw lithium concentrate exports with a full ban on unprocessed material beginning next year.

headline: WHY INSTITUTIONAL FORECASTERS STILL SEE GOLD AT $5,000 DESPITE MAY'S BRUTAL SELLOFF
snippet: Despite gold retreating nearly 20% from its Q1 2026 record near $5,600/oz, major banks including Goldman Sachs and Citi maintain $5,000+ targets for year-end 2026, citing durable structural support: central bank accumulation at multi-decade highs, US debt trajectory concerns, de-dollarization momentum, and a persistent Middle East geopolitical risk premium. The structural bull case for gold hasn't changed — the price has.

headline: GOLD AND SILVER MINING STOCKS AWAIT A CATALYST — THIS WEEK IN MINING
snippet: GoldSeek's weekly mining roundup finds gold and silver equities technically oversold but lacking a near-term catalyst to break higher after a bruising week for precious metals. The issue surveys producer earnings, junior explorer drill results, and commodity price technicals, with the next directional move expected to hinge on US inflation data and the Fed's next signal on rate policy. China's silver imports exceeding 790 tonnes in early 2026 remain a structural demand positive.
